question.problem:
Consider the vectors $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_2$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2 \times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14245038/assets/566569dbf0d6373b8482b41bc6fbc8b69d77eaf0cf5987151fe3854c77de9219.svg)
The vectors $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_2$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues $\lambda_1=2$ and $\lambda_2=1-\textrm{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PBP^{-1},$ find the matrix $P.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\color{red}\lambda_1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${\color{red}{\mathbf{v}_1}},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\color{blue}\lambda_2} = \overline{\color{blue}\lambda}_{\color{blue}3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_2} = \overline{\color{blue}\mathbf{v}}_{\color{blue}3},$ then $A=PBP^{-1},$ where
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14245038/assets/7e33a1ba83b16d1b5767ee773aaa5d797eaab72949e98bb51aed6fbd249ab386.svg)
Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14245038/assets/22f1869f42a464e5d682ae6e7b5b33c75b8a1d480869baa5fc036ffaaa4d8417.svg)
we deduce that the first column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${{\color{red}{\mathbf{v}_1}}},$ and the second and third columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_2} .$ Therefore, 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14245038/assets/b1f00ea903f35490283b270c21eb49e4934235a2173a0d3b25c8feac6a6a509d.svg)
